The word that came from the Lord to Isaiah, son of Amos, concerning Judah and Jerusalem. It seems that the previous words were related to the present ones through similar ideas. For the words that came from God to the prophet in the past were about Judah and Jerusalem. It appears that the vision has a somewhat unclear and intermediate meaning concerning Judah and Jerusalem. As we clarify the power of the vision, we bring it to mind in a concise manner. For the prophecy speaks about the sensible Judah and Jerusalem, and also about the spiritual and intelligible ones in Christ. The vision is said to be about Judah and Jerusalem, not against them, but concerning them. We call Judah and Jerusalem sensible, referring to the land where Israel dwelled and the system of the Jewish synagogue. Again, we consider the intelligible Jerusalem, or Judah, to be the Church, that is, the spiritual circumcision, which is the circumcision of the heart, not made by hands, and the people who have it in mind and heart.

The divine Paul knows another Jew, not the one according to flesh, but the one in spirit. He writes that the one in the visible is not a Jew, nor is circumcision in the visible in flesh, but the one in the hidden is a Jew, and circumcision of the heart, in spirit, not in letter, whose praise is not from humans, but from God. Therefore, it is necessary to observe carefully when the prophet speaks against Jerusalem, that is, Judaea, and when about the one in Christ and intelligible, which is truly perfect and blameless. What does he say? That in the last days, the mountain of the Lord will be visible, and the house of God will be on the tops of the mountains. And it will be exalted above the hills, and all nations will come to it. And many nations will go and say: Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord…
pass_b_english: The word that came from the Lord to Isaiah, son of Amos, concerns Judah and Jerusalem. It seems that the previous words were related to the present ones through similar ideas, for words once came from God to the prophet regarding Judah and Jerusalem.

It appears that the vision has a somewhat intermediate and not very clear meaning in its delivery concerning Judah and Jerusalem. As we clarify the power of the vision, we bring it to mind in a concise manner. Because the prophecy attempts to speak of the sensible Judah and Jerusalem, it also reveals the intelligible and spiritual one in Christ, and makes it manifest in this world; for this reason, the vision is said to be about Judah and Jerusalem, not against Judah, nor indeed against Jerusalem, but concerning Judah and Jerusalem.

We call Judah and Jerusalem sensible, referring to the land where Israel dwelled and the system of the Jewish synagogue. Again, we consider the intelligible Jerusalem, or Judah, to be the Church—that is, the spiritual circumcision, which is the circumcision of the heart, being the people who have the unmade circumcision in Christ in mind and heart.

Indeed, one of the holy prophets once proclaimed to the Jews: 'Circumcise yourselves to God, and circumcise the hardness of our hearts, O men of Judah and you who dwell in Jerusalem' (Jeremiah 4:4). The divine Paul knows another Jew, not the one according to the flesh, but the one in the spirit. He writes: 'For the one is not a Jew who is one outwardly, nor is circumcision outward in the flesh; but he is a Jew who is one inwardly, and circumcision is of the heart, in the spirit, not in the letter, whose praise is not from men, but from God' (Romans 2:28-29).

Therefore, it is necessary to observe carefully, since the prophet sometimes makes words against Jerusalem, that is, Judah, and sometimes about the one in Christ and the intelligible, which is truly perfect and blameless. What, then, does he say? That in the last days the mountain of the Lord will be made manifest, and the house of God will be on the tops of the mountains. It will be exalted above the hills, and all nations will come to it. And many nations will go and say: 'Come, let us go up to the mountain of the Lord...' (Isaiah 2:2-3).
